title: Fix unauthorized error on chunked upload start

requirements.summary: Verify that the frontend actor is constructed with the authenticated identity (not anonymous) when the user is logged in via Internet Identity before calling startUpload.
acceptanceCriteria: After login via Internet Identity, the actor used for upload calls carries the authenticated principal.
The startUpload call is made with the authenticated actor, not an anonymous one.
No Unauthorized error appears in the browser console during a PDF upload attempt by a logged-in user.

file_operations.description: Review the actor creation logic to ensure that when an authenticated identity is available from the InternetIdentity context, the actor is constructed with that identity rather than anonymously. Verify that the actor invalidation and recreation occurs properly when the user logs in, so that subsequent backend calls (including startUpload) use the authenticated principal. If the actor is cached or created before authentication completes, ensure it is rebuilt after login.

Review the useStartUpload hook and other upload-related query hooks (useUploadChunk, useFinalizeUpload) to confirm they are using the actor from useActor and that the actor is not being overridden or replaced with an anonymous actor. Ensure that these hooks correctly depend on the authenticated actor so that startUpload, uploadChunk, and finalizeUpload are called with the authenticated identity. Add error handling to display a user-friendly message if an 'Unauthorized' error occurs.

Ensure that the UploadPage checks for user authentication before allowing a file upload. If the user is not authenticated, display a prompt or redirect to login. Verify that the upload flow (startUpload, uploadChunk, finalizeUpload) is initiated only after the authenticated actor is available. Add visual feedback or error messages if an authorization error occurs during the upload process.
